STEP 1 - Scene: A single small piece of corn on the cob on a white square plate, photographed from above (the image is rotated 90°).

STEP 2 - Ruler: The square plate is about 24 cm across, so its area is roughly 24 × 24 × 0.85 ≈ 490 cm² (rounded corners).

STEP 3 - Items: One corn cob segment, cooked, with maybe a faint trace of butter or moisture.

STEP 4 - Area: The corn is about 80 px by 95 px in an image where the plate is about 440 px wide, which gives roughly 0.055 cm per px... more precisely 24 cm / 440 px ≈ 0.055 cm/px. That makes the corn about 4.4 cm long by 5.2 cm across (the diameter is probably about 4.5 cm). Its footprint is about 4.4 × 4.5 ≈ 20 cm², about 4% of the plate. The total food coverage is therefore about 4%.

STEP 5 - Volume: A cylinder 4.5 cm in diameter and 4.4 cm long has a volume of π × 2.25² × 4.4 ≈ 70 ml. This includes the cob.

STEP 6 - Grams: The density of corn on the cob is about 0.9 g/ml, so the weight is about 63 g. That is cob plus kernels.

STEP 7 - Energy: Corn on the cob has about 96 kcal per 100 g, including the cob, so 63 g gives about 60 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A 4–5 cm corn piece weighing about 60 g is plausible. The plate is mostly empty, which matches the small total.
